bugs.what: Cinderhall/Iron Downs was referenced by ~6 different NPCs (Tamsin's quest, Warder Iss, Ironbound talk, the Regent's herald's hold list, the late-game 'Column' quest) but no room ever exposed a direct path there; extensive exploration of Thornwold's forest fringes (Spoil Verge, Deer Break, Black Thorn Stand, etc.) never surfaced an exit toward it.

Failed forced-check actions (e.g. 'drag the skiff free', 'talk him into leaving') raise their own DC by 1 per miss with no in-fiction alternative offered, which can spiral a stat-mismatched build (Scholar's low might/grace) toward a near-unwinnable grind on an optional but plot-relevant action.
bugs.where: Fenmarch Ironbound Mission skiff / Hollowbrook Robbed Mounds

bugs.what: The 'name it' free/no-roll pacify option appeared on nearly every 'armor useless' undead-guard encounter (gray husk, barrow-wight x2, gray sergeant, grave-wight, honour guard) and always worked with zero cost, trivializing what the room textframed as dangerous, mail-piercing threats.

confusions: No signposted route to the Iron Downs/Cinderhall despite it being a named, quest-critical destination mentioned by multiple NPCs across two hubs.

The Hollow Throne room's four ending paths (rite/burn/bargain/crown/read-ledger) are only summarized via a free 'weigh' action after arriving there — a first-time player without that free-look habit could stumble into 'kneel' (an instant loss condition) without realizing its weight.
suggestions: Add an explicit travel connector (or at least a 'toward the Iron Downs' room exit) from one of Thornwold's known hub rooms once the relevant quest is picked up.
Cap or soften escalating DCs on optional-but-narratively-interesting forced actions, or surface the 'ask a companion for help' option sooner for might/grace checks a Scholar build is weak in.
Vary the undead-guardian encounters so 'name it' isn't a universal free pass — e.g. limit it to one enemy type, or give the guardians distinct pacify conditions tied to the room's specific lore.
status/look tool is excellent for orientation — keep surfacing it proactively (e.g. auto-suggest 'weigh' options) at other point-of-no-return rooms like the Pass Gate.
